claims.statement: The EU DPP Registry entered testing in July 2026, and passports become mandatory on 18 February 2027 for specified EV, light-transport, home-storage, and industrial batteries.
The economic operator placing the finished battery on the market must create and maintain the passport, making its compliance or product-data budget the likely payer.
A passport operator needs manufacturer data rights and compliant registry interoperability; neither is currently acquired.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Battery product, compliance, or operations director
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: Large product-lifecycle platforms can bundle DPP; a Poland-focused connector for storage assemblers and importers is the wedge
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: Unknown today; proposed direct contracts with battery assemblers and importers
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Battery testing labs, renewable installers, industry associations, and direct outreach

fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Implementation milestones prepaid; annual hosting in advance
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Assumption: 60-80% after data onboarding and support
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Assumption: 80-300 implementation hours per product family
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Security, standards conformance, product-liability boundaries, backups, and legal review
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Implementation plus annual fee by passport or SKU volume
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Identifiers, storage, registry calls, data validation, and support

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: PLM, ERP, certification, and traceability vendors add battery-passport modules
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Current engineering and compliance labor mapping product data into the now-live test infrastructure before the February 2027 mandate
commercial_mechanics.payer: Economic operator placing covered finished batteries on the EU market
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: Registry testing, customer tender, or inability to assemble mandatory fields before launch
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Annual hosting plus passport updates throughout battery life

contrary_evidence: Detailed implementation elements continued arriving in 2026, raising scope uncertainty.
Large manufacturers may build internally or use established PLM vendors.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Proposed data-rights agreement granting product-record ingestion and passport maintenance authority; unsigned
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Sell a schema-readiness assessment and export package without hosting passports
critical_control_point.current_owner: Battery economic operators own product data; the EU controls registry infrastructure
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: Unknown today; proposed direct contracts with battery assemblers and importers
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: Public test documentation can support prototyping, but no manufacturer data rights exist
critical_control_point.launch_controller: Prospective business after customer mandate; economic operator remains legally responsible
critical_control_point.renewal: Proposed multi-year hosting with annual renewal; unsigned
critical_control_point.subject: Manufacturer-authorized battery passport record and maintenance right

economics.acquisition_route: Build against the registry test environment, sell readiness audits to storage importers, then onboard one product family
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Assumption: 100 operators averaging 100,000 PLN annual recurring revenue yields 10m PLN ARR; specialist costs still permit a possible 5m PLN founder net-worth path in 6-10 years. Market concentration and implementation effort are unknown.
economics.founder_time: 20-25 hours weekly until implementation staff are hired
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hosting and maintenance revenue less onboarding, validation, and compliance support
economics.payback: Assumption: 12-18 months because acquisition and implementation are enterprise-heavy
economics.pricing: Assumption: 30,000-150,000 PLN implementation plus 2-10 PLN per passport annually subject to minimum
economics.retention_or_repeat: Multi-year records updated through the battery lifecycle

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Reusable connectors and field-quality benchmarks across battery supply chains
fingerprint.customer: EU battery storage assemblers and importers
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Battery-passport implementation and hosted data service
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Economic operator pays engineering and compliance labor to create mandatory passports
fingerprint.problem_trigger: The registry is live for testing shortly before the first mandatory date

founder_fit: Renewable-energy context offers domain adjacency without assuming family data rights.
Data engineering fits the founder's technical training.
High-value B2B work can start with a bounded readiness audit.
risks: Standards and access rules may still change.
Enterprise implementations may exceed part-time capacity.
Incumbent PLM vendors have strong integration advantages.

structural_signature.critical_dependency_descriptor: eu registry and final technical rule compatibility

structure.control_point: Maintained passport record for each battery
structure.critical_dependency: Manufacturer data rights and registry conformance

thesis: The live registry and near mandate create a time-bounded implementation market among smaller battery operators lacking enterprise PLM capability.
title: Battery Passport Operator for Storage SMEs
uncertainties: Number of reachable small operators is unknown.
Final service-provider obligations may affect cost.
